title: A Parasite Makes Rats Walk Straight Up to Cats

scenes.text: Some rats walk straight up to a cat. On purpose.
A healthy rat smells a cat and runs. These rats sniff cat urine and move closer.
The reason is a parasite, Toxoplasma. In the rat's brain it packs twice as many cysts into the fear center as anywhere else.
It has a plan. The parasite can only breed inside a cat's gut. So it needs its rat to get eaten.
Oxford scientists named it fatal attraction. The rat dies, the parasite moves in, the cycle starts again.
And the CDC says over 40 million Americans carry the same parasite. So, which way would you walk?

description:
A parasite called Toxoplasma gondii makes infected rats lose their fear of cats and even approach cat urine.
Oxford scientists called it fatal attraction in 2000; the parasite concentrates its cysts in the amygdala, the brain's fear center, and can only reproduce inside a cat, so a rat that gets eaten is exactly what it needs. The CDC says more than 40 million people in the United States carry the parasite.
What is the creepiest parasite you know?

first_comment: The parasite can only breed inside a cat, so it rewires the rat to get eaten. Which animal parasite do you think is the most disturbing?
